responsibilities.label: Storage infrastructure
responsibilities.explanation: The provider runs the file-storage system. Object storage stores files with identifying names and descriptive information, usually in groups called buckets. Reliable storage does not protect against your own deletions, stolen access keys or incorrect rules for keeping files.

responsibilities.label: Access rules
responsibilities.explanation: Choose who can read or change each file, check permissions in your app and use temporary access where needed. Avoid public file collections or permanent access keys when users should see only their own files.

responsibilities.label: File delivery network
responsibilities.explanation: A content delivery network (CDN) keeps copies of files near visitors. Excluded means you connect a separate delivery product, not that one cannot be used. You still decide who can access cached files and when old copies must be replaced.

responsibilities.label: Keeping and restoring files
responsibilities.explanation: Choose how long to keep files and how to recover them. Depending on the product, this may mean keeping old versions, allowing deleted files to be restored or making independent copies. Test recovery; not every product supports every option.

responsibilities.label: Harmful-file checks
responsibilities.explanation: This comparison covers storage itself. Checking files for harmful software or prohibited content, and displaying uploads safely, requires separate tools or connected products, even when the same provider sells them.
